correctness.rationale: For every real input on a finite positively weighted tree, coarea reduces one-input weighted variation gain to neighborhood-perimeter ratios. A unique-tree-path charging argument bounds every dilated cut boundary by weighted oriented waves of its original cut edges; deleting one edge and indicating the opposite component attains each ratio. The one-step degree/weight characterization, BFS degree bound and finite-radius collapse are proved analytically. Independently executed standalone verifier checked 1,628 sharp cut comparisons (318,280 candidate indicator sets) across 304 weighted trees, plus 11,309 integer-signal inequalities and 12 branching constructions; finite checks corroborate but do not prove the universal theorem.

value.rationale: For a natural nonlinear graph filtering operator, a priori variation growth could require searching exponentially many input cuts. The theorem identifies every sharp radius gain by only oriented edge frontiers and constructs exact extremizers. It detects a rigid one-step contraction class and transient exponential growth despite eventual constant-output behavior, which is a substantive structural contrast relevant to graph morphology and stable signal processing.
